mainTopic: Who counts as the נשיא; the anointed כהן גדול; the שמן המשחה and when kings and כהנים גדולים are anointed
overview: The amud opens by finishing a גזירה שוה: the נשיא who brings a שעיר is a ruler with only ה׳ above him, just like a king. רבי asks רבי חייא whether he himself qualifies. רבי חייא says no, because the ראש גולה in בבל has authority over ארץ ישראל. In רב ספרא's version, the reason is that the ראש גולה holds the 'שבט' of real power, while הלל's descendants hold only the 'מחוקק' of teaching Torah. A new משנה then defines the כהן משיח as the one anointed with שמן המשחה. It also lists how he differs from a מרובה בגדים, and how a serving כהן גדול differs from a former one. The גמרא brings ברייתות about how the שמן המשחה was made and the miracles of its twelve לוגין. It then explains why a כהן גדול's son must be anointed but a king's son is anointed only when there is a dispute, and why only kings of בית דוד are anointed. Finally, it clears up the order and names of יאשיהו's sons, ending with why צדקיהו was also called שלום and how he got the name צדקיהו.

steps.title: The נשיא is one with only ה׳ above him
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה ends: just as the king has no one above him except ה׳, so too the נשיא who brings a שעיר has no one above him except ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there (with the king) it means someone who has only ה׳ his God above him, so too a נשיא means someone who has only ה׳ his God above him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a comparison it started before this point. It defines which 'נשיא' brings the special שעיר offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ה׳ אלהיו' appear both about the king and about the נשיא. So the same definition carries over: the נשיא is a supreme ruler with no human authority over him. A lower official does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there (in the other פסוק)
The ruler who brings a male goat as his חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: A נשיא who brings a שעיר must be a ruler with no one above him except ה׳, just like a king.
steps.whyThisMatters: This definition sets up the next question: does רבי, the נשיא of ארץ ישראל, really have no one above him?

phrases.english: Just as there, where there is no one above him
phrases.notes: 'There' is the פסוק about the king, which also uses the words 'ה׳ אלהיו' (דברים 17:19).

phrases.english: except the Lord his God,
so too a נשיא, over whom there is no one
phrases.notes: The נשיא's פסוק says 'מכל מצות ה׳ אלהיו' (ויקרא 4:22).

phrases.english: except the Lord his God.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן שֶׁאֵין עַל גַּבָּיו אֶלָּא ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the גזירה שוה that began before this text.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The נשיא of the שעיר offering is a supreme ruler answerable only to ה׳.

steps.title: רבי asks if he would bring a שעיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא asks רבי חייא whether someone like him counts as a נשיא for the שעיר offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי asked רבי חייא: Someone like me, what is the law? Would I bring a goat?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks a real practical question about himself. Does he, the נשיא in ארץ ישראל, fit the definition from Step 1?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the נשיא must have only ה׳ above him. רבי is the leader in ארץ ישראל, so he wants to know if he qualifies, or if he brings a regular person's female animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi asked Rabbi Chiyya:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the leader of the Jews in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Someone like me, what is the law regarding a goat?
phrases.notes: He's asking: if I sin by mistake, do I bring the נשיא's male goat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the definition from Step 1 to a real person.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי, as נשיא of ארץ ישראל, bring a שעיר?

steps.title: Your rival is in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that רבי does not qualify, because the ראש גולה in בבל is a rival ruler.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your rival is in Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers no. רבי is not the only top leader, because the ראש גולה in בבל also leads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is another ruler as great as you, you are not a sole ruler with only ה׳ above you. So רבי would bring a regular person's offering.

phrases.english: He said to him: Your rival is in Babylonia.
phrases.notes: The rival is the ראש גולה, the leader of the Jews in בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, because the ראש גולה is an equal rival, so רבי is not a sole ruler.

steps.title: Two sets of kings both brought a שעיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי objects: kings of Israel and kings of the house of David ruled at the same time, yet each brought a king's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: Kings of Israel and kings of the house of David, these bring for themselves and those bring for themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes back on רבי חייא's answer with a ברייתא. Having a rival does not seem to cancel the special offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings of Israel and the kings of Judah each ruled at the same time. Each still counted as a king and brought a שעיר. So why should the ראש גולה stop רבי from counting?

keyTerms.meaning: Kings of the northern kingdom of Israel
Kings of the house of David (Judah)

phrases.english: He raised an objection: kings of Israel
and kings of the house of David,
these bring for themselves,
and those bring for themselves!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that having a rival ruler stops someone from counting as a נשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two kings ruling at once both brought a שעיר, so a rival alone cannot cancel the status.

steps.title: Here we are under their authority
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers: those kings were not under each other, but the Jews of ארץ ישראל are under the ראש גולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, they were not subject to each other. Here, we are subject to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא explains the difference. It is not just having a rival; it is being under someone's power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two kings were each fully independent. The ראש גולה actually has authority over the people in ארץ ישראל. So רבי has someone above him and is not a sole ruler.
steps.whatToRemember: The key test is not having a rival but being under someone else's authority.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָא כַּיְיפִי אַהֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: He said to him: There, they were not subject to each other,
here, we are subject to them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the ראש גולה in בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends Step 3 against the objection in Step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rival ruler cancels נשיא status, which seemed to clash with the two kings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only being under another's authority cancels it; independent kings each count.

steps.title: רב ספרא's version: the same question
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא tells the story another way, starting with the same question from רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא taught it this way: רבי asked רבי חייא: Someone like me, what is the law regarding a goat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same conversation. The question stays the same; the answer will be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the question on purpose, because רב ספרא remembers a different reply from רבי חייא. This sets up the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Safra taught it this way.
Rabbi asked Rabbi Chiyya:
Someone like me, what is the law regarding a goat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the story in a second version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Same question: does רבי bring a שעיר?

steps.title: There a scepter, here a staff
steps.stepSummary: In this version רבי חייא answers that the ראש גולה holds a 'שבט' (scepter), while רבי holds only a 'מחוקק' (staff).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it is a 'scepter'; here, it is a 'staff'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers with words from a פסוק. The ראש גולה has the stronger kind of rule, and רבי has a lesser kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is not 'you have a rival'. It is that רבי's rule is a lower level of power than the ראש גולה's, so he is not a top ruler.

keyTerms.meaning: Staff of a lawgiver or teacher

phrases.english: He said to him: There, a 'scepter';
phrases.notes: 'There' is בבל, where the ראש גולה rules.

phrases.english: here, a 'staff'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in the second version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, because the ראש גולה holds real ruling power and רבי holds a lesser kind.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains scepter and staff
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'שבט' as the ראש גולה who rules with a rod, and 'מחוקק' as the descendants of הלל who teach Torah in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: 'The scepter shall not depart from Judah' — this is the ראש גולה in Babylonia, who rules Israel with a rod. 'Nor the staff from between his feet' — these are the descendants of הלל, who teach Torah to Israel in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי חייא's answer. It shows what 'שבט' and 'מחוקק' mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש גולה can force the people to obey ('with a rod'). The family of הלל, which includes רבי, leads by teaching Torah. So the נשיא in ארץ ישראל is not the supreme ruler.

keyTerms.meaning: Leader of the Jews in exile

steps.whatToRemember: In רב ספרא's version, the ראש גולה rules with power ('שבט'), while רבי's family leads by teaching Torah ('מחוקק'), so רבי does not bring a שעיר.

phrases.english: And it is taught: 'The scepter shall not depart from Judah' —
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:10

phrases.english: this is the Exilarch in Babylonia,
who rules over Israel with a rod.
'Nor the staff from between his feet' —
these are the descendants of Hillel
who teach Torah to Israel in public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the ראש גולה's rule is greater than the נשיא's in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: New משנה: who is the anointed כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the כהן משיח as the כהן גדול anointed with שמן המשחה, not one who became כהן גדול by wearing the extra garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And who is the anointed one? The one anointed with the anointing oil, not the one with extra garments.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and turns to the כהן גדול. It explains which כהן גדול the תורה calls 'משיח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some כהנים גדולים were anointed with שמן המשחה. Others, after the oil was no longer available, became כהן גדול just by wearing the eight special garments. Only the anointed one counts as the 'משיח' for these laws.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול made so by wearing the extra garments

phrases.english: MISHNA: And who is the anointed one?
The one anointed with the anointing oil,
not the one with extra garments.
phrases.notes: This is a כהן גדול who was put into office by wearing the special garments, without the oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן משיח is only the one anointed with שמן המשחה.

steps.title: The only difference: the פר for all the מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the only difference between an anointed כהן גדול and a מרובה בגדים is the פר brought for a mistaken sin in any of the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difference between a כהן anointed with the anointing oil and one with extra garments, except the bull that comes for all the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists what separates the two kinds of כהן גדול. Only the anointed one brings the special bull for a mistaken sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In everything else they are the same. But the bull (פר כהן משיח) belongs only to the anointed one, which is why Step 9 defined 'משיח' so carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought for a mistake in any of the מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין בין' does not mean the two are different in many ways. It means they are the same in everything except the one thing listed.

phrases.english: There is no difference between a priest anointed
with the anointing oil and one with extra garments,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פַּר הַבָּא עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת.
phrases.english: except the bull that comes for all the מצוות.
phrases.notes: This is the bull a כהן משיח brings after ruling wrongly and acting on it by mistake (ויקרא 4:3).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן הַמָּשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה לִמְרוּבֵּה בְּגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical difference behind Step 9's definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the anointed כהן גדול brings the פר for a mistaken sin; otherwise the two are equal.

steps.title: The two differences between a serving and a former כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a serving כהן גדול differs from a former one only in the פר of יום הכיפורים and the עשירית האיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only difference between the כהן גדול who is serving now and a former כהן גדול is the bull of יום הכיפורים and the tenth of an איפה offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of differences. Now it compares the current כהן גדול with a כהן גדול who used to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the current כהן גדול brings two offerings: the פר יום הכיפורים and the daily עשירית האיפה. Everything else stays the same for both of them, and the next line spells that out.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול who is serving right now
A former כהן גדול, one who filled in for a while
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכיפורים
The flour offering the כהן גדול brings every day

phrases.english: And there is no difference between a serving כהן
and a כהן who has passed
phrases.notes: This is someone who filled in as כהן גדול while the regular one couldn't serve, and then stepped back down.

phrases.english: except the bull of יום הכיפורים
and the tenth of an איפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's pattern of 'אין בין': step 10 compared two kinds of כהן גדול, and this step compares a serving one with a former one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the serving כהן גדול brings the פר יום הכיפורים and the עשירית האיפה.

steps.title: What the serving and former כהן גדול share
steps.stepSummary: Both kinds of כהן גדול are equal in the יום הכיפורים service and in all the special כהן גדול restrictions, and both of their deaths free the accidental killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them are equal in the יום הכיפורים service. Both must marry a בתולה and may not marry an אלמנה. Neither may become טמא for a relative. Neither may let his hair grow long or tear his clothes in mourning. When either one dies, the accidental killer goes back home.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists all the laws that the current and the former כהן גדול have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A former כהן גדול keeps the status of a כהן גדול. All the personal rules of a כהן גדול still apply to him, and so does the law of returning the רוצח. Only the two offerings from the last step belong to the serving כהן גדול alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The special Temple service of יום הכיפורים
Letting the hair grow long in mourning
They bring the accidental killer back home from the עיר מקלט

steps.whatToRemember: Both kinds of כהן גדול share every rule of the כהן גדול. The only difference is the two offerings that the serving כהן גדול brings.

phrases.english: This one and that one are equal
in the service of יום הכיפורים,
and they are commanded about marrying a virgin,
and they are forbidden to a widow,
and they do not become impure for their relatives,
and they do not grow their hair long, and they do not tear their clothes,
and they bring back the killer.
phrases.notes: When a כהן גדול dies, someone who killed by accident may leave the עיר מקלט and go home.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִים בַּעֲבוֹדַת יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison by listing everything the two kinds of כהן גדול share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A former כהן גדול shares every law of the serving כהן גדול apart from the two offerings.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the roots were boiled in the oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says that to make the שמן המשחה, the spice roots were boiled in the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. The רבנן taught: the שמן המשחה that משה made in the desert was made by boiling the spice roots in it. This is what רבי יהודה says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא about how משה prepared the שמן המשחה. The משנה had mentioned this oil when it described the כהן משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה describes the method in a simple way: the roots were cooked right in the oil. This opinion sets up the argument that comes next.

phrases.english: גמרא. The רבנן taught:
The anointing oil that משה made in the desert:
they would boil the roots in it,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה בַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a ברייתא about the שמן המשחה, which the משנה mentioned in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the spice roots were boiled directly in the oil.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: there was too little oil, so water was used
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי objects that the oil was not enough even to coat the roots. He says the roots were soaked in water, and the oil floated on top and picked up the smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Isn't the oil not even enough to smear on the roots? Rather, they soak the roots in water, float the oil on top of the water, and the oil picks up the smell. Then they skim the oil off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי challenges רבי יהודה's method and offers a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roots would soak up the whole small amount of oil, so there would be none left to boil them in. Roots that are already full of water do not absorb oil. So the oil only takes in the smell from the water, and then it is removed.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא לָסוּךְ אֶת הָעִקָּרִים אֵינוֹ סוֹפֵק?!
phrases.english: But isn't it not enough even to smear the roots?!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the amount of oil משה made.

phrases.english: Rather: they soak the roots in water,
and he floats oil on top of it,
and it picks up the smell, and he skims it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא לָסוּךְ אֶת הָעִקָּרִים אֵינוֹ סוֹפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהודה's boiling method and replaces it with a water method.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the roots were boiled in the oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The small amount of oil would be completely absorbed by the roots, so there would be nothing left to boil them in.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: this oil was full of miracles anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the שמן המשחה involved many miracles, so it is no problem if making it also needed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Was only one miracle done with the שמן המשחה? It started as just twelve לוגין. With it they anointed the משכן and its כלים, and אהרן and his sons, all seven days of the מילואים. And all of it is still here for the future, as the פסוק says: 'This shall be a holy anointing oil for Me for your generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה defends his opinion. He points out that this oil was miraculous from start to finish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that there was not naturally enough oil. But twelve לוגין anointed so much and still never ran out, so the oil clearly worked by miracle. One more miracle when it was made fits that picture.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven days when the משכן was set up and the כהנים were put into their jobs

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not deny that there was too little oil. He answers that the whole story of the שמן המשחה is a story of miracles.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי נֵס אֶחָד נַעֲשָׂה בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה?
phrases.english: Was only one miracle done with the anointing oil?
But at the start it was only twelve לוגין,
and from it the משכן and its vessels were anointed,

phrases.aramaic: אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו כׇּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמִּלּוּאִים,
phrases.english: and אהרן and his sons, all seven days of the inauguration,
and all of it remains for the future,
as it says: 'A holy anointing oil
this shall be to Me for your generations.'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:31

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי נֵס אֶחָד נַעֲשָׂה בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's objection and keeps רבי יהודה's boiling method.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the natural problem but explains it as a miracle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because there was too little oil, boiling the roots in it could not have worked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oil worked by miracle at every stage, so a miracle when it was made is also expected.

steps.title: The many miracles of the anointing oil
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: רבי יהודה says the שמן המשחה began as only twelve לוגין, yet it lasted for every anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches about the פסוק 'And משה took the anointing oil and anointed the משכן and everything in it.' רבי יהודה says the oil משה made in the desert had many miracles from beginning to end. It started as only twelve לוגין. Think how much oil the pot soaks up, how much the roots soak up, and how much the fire burns off. Yet with this oil they anointed the משכן and its vessels, and אהרן and his sons for all seven days of the מילואים. Later כהנים גדולים and kings were anointed with it too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא from רבי יהודה. It backs up his earlier claim that the שמן המשחה was full of miracles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, רבי יהודה said a miracle in making the oil is no problem, because the oil was miraculous anyway. Here he spells out what he meant. A small amount of oil should have shrunk even more while it was being made, yet it was enough for every anointing for generations.

keyTerms.meaning: לוגין, a unit of liquid measure
The seven days when the משכן and the כהנים were inaugurated

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"And Moses took the anointing oil
and anointed the Tabernacle and all that was in it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:10

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The anointing oil that Moses made in the wilderness,

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ בּוֹ מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף,
phrases.english: how many miracles were done with it, from beginning to end!

phrases.aramaic: תְּחִלָּתוֹ לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר לוּגִּין,
phrases.english: At the start it was only twelve log.
Look how much a pot soaks up,
and how much the roots soak up,
and how much the fire burns off,

phrases.aramaic: וּבוֹ נִמְשַׁח מִשְׁכָּן וְכֵלָיו וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו
phrases.english: and yet with it the Tabernacle, its vessels, Aaron and his sons were anointed
for all seven days of the inauguration,
and with it High Priests and kings were anointed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'many miracles' that רבי יהודה mentioned in his answer in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twelve לוגין of שמן המשחה miraculously lasted for all the anointings, from the משכן through later כהנים גדולים and kings.

steps.title: Who needs anointing: a high priest's son yes, a king's son no
steps.stepSummary: Even a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול must be anointed, but a מלך who is the son of a מלך is not anointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול needs to be anointed. But we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא was just talking about anointing כהנים גדולים and kings. Now it adds two rules about when anointing is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two positions work differently. Being כהן גדול does not pass down by itself, so every new כהן גדול must be anointed. Being king does pass down, so a king's son usually takes over without anointing.

keyTerms.meaning: A king who is the son of a king

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. A כהן גדול's son still needs oil, but a king's son does not.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: And even a High Priest who is the son of a High Priest
requires anointing,
but we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of anointing כהנים גדולים and kings in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול needs anointing. A king who is the son of a king does not.

steps.title: But שלמה, a king's son, was anointed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own rule: why was שלמה anointed if he was the son of King דוד?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will ask: why did they anoint שלמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem with the rule it just gave. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה was the son of King דוד, so by the rule he should not have needed oil. Yet the פסוקים say he was anointed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up a problem)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
Why did they anoint Solomon?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from Step 17 that a king's son is not anointed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a king who is the son of a king is not anointed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה was a king's son, yet he was anointed.

steps.title: Anointing was needed because of a rival claim
steps.stepSummary: שלמה, יואש and יהואחז were each anointed because someone else challenged their right to rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה was anointed because of the challenge from אדוניה. יואש was anointed because of עתליה. יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, who was two years older than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the problem from Step 18. It also lists two more kings' sons who were anointed, and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these kings had a rival who claimed the throne. The anointing showed clearly who was the rightful king. So these cases are exceptions caused by the dispute, and the basic rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: His dispute, a challenge to his right to rule

phrases.english: Because of the challenge of Adonijah,
and Joash because of Athaliah,
and Jehoahaz because of Jehoiakim,
who was two years older than him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: it applies only when no one disputes who should be king.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה's anointing seems to go against the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: When someone disputes who should be king, even a king's son is anointed.

steps.title: The same oil will last into the future
steps.stepSummary: The twelve לוגין of oil still exist for the future, as the word זה hints.
steps.simpleTranslation: That same oil will still exist in the future, as the פסוק says: 'This shall be holy anointing oil to Me for your generations.' The word זה has the number value of twelve, which hints at the twelve לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of miracles. The oil was never used up and will remain for the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For your generations' shows the oil lasts. The word זה ('this') points to the same exact twelve לוגין משה made. That fits the miracle that the oil never ran out.

keyTerms.meaning: The number value of Hebrew letters

steps.whatToRemember: The miracles of the שמן המשחה: only twelve לוגין, enough for every anointing, and still whole for the future.

phrases.english: And that oil still exists for the future,
as it is said: "Holy anointing oil
this shall be to Me for your generations."
phrases.notes: שמות 30:31

phrases.english: "This" [zeh], by its number value,
is twelve log.
phrases.notes: ז is 7 and ה is 5, which adds up to 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of miracles from Step 16, after the side point about who gets anointed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original twelve לוגין of oil remain for the future, hinted in the word זה.

steps.title: Source that a high priest's son needs anointing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול still needs anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that even a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול needs anointing. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the ברייתא's rules and asks for a source for each one. This step asks about the first rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a כהן גדול's son simply takes over from his father, the way a king's son does. So the גמרא wants a פסוק showing he still needs oil.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה.
phrases.english: And even a High Priest who is the son of a High Priest requires anointing.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts looking at the ברייתא's rule from Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that a כהן גדול's son must be anointed.

steps.title: The extra word 'anointed' in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The word המשיח in 'the anointed כהן who takes his place from his sons' teaches that even a son becomes כהן גדול only through anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And the anointed כהן who takes his place from among his sons.' The פסוק could have just said 'the כהן who takes his place from among his sons.' Why add 'anointed'? To teach that even a son of a כהן גדול is כהן גדול only if he is anointed. If he is not anointed, he is not כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It points to a word that seems extra and learns the rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From his sons' already tells us the son takes over. Adding 'anointed' shows that being the son is not enough. Anointing is what makes him כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק say (it could have said)

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the anointed priest in his place from among his sons."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:15

phrases.english: Let the verse say: "And the priest in his place from among his sons."
Why add "the anointed"?

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּמִבָּנָיו דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: It teaches us that from the sons of a High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָוֵי מָשִׁיחַ – הָוֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: if he is anointed, he is a High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – לָא הָוֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: and if not, he is not a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word המשיח teaches that anointing, not being the son, makes him כהן גדול.

steps.title: Source that a king's son is not anointed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that a king who is the son of a king is not anointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second rule of the ברייתא and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a כהן גדול's son does need oil, the opposite rule for kings needs its own source.

phrases.english: The Master said:
But we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְאֵין מוֹשְׁחִין מֶלֶךְ בֶּן מֶלֶךְ. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהן גדול rule to the king rule of Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that a king's son takes over without anointing.

steps.title: The kingdom is an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns from 'so he may lengthen his days in his kingdom, he and his sons' that kingship is inherited.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: it is written, 'So that he may lengthen his days on his kingdom' and so on. This means the kingdom is an inheritance for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a פסוק as the source for the king rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to say 'he and his sons.' That shows the kingdom passes down to the son automatically. Since the son inherits it, he does not need anointing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said: As it is written:
"So that he may lengthen his days in his kingdom, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:20. The rest of the פסוק says 'he and his sons,' and that's the key part.

phrases.english: It is an inheritance for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kingship is an inheritance, so the son takes over without anointing.

steps.title: Source that a dispute requires anointing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that in a dispute the king's son needs anointing, and a king cannot simply hand the throne to any son he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when there is a dispute, anointing is needed, and that a king cannot pass the kingdom to whichever son he wants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the exception from Step 19, where kings' sons were anointed because of a rival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in Step 24 seems to say kingship always passes down. So the גמרא wants to know where the Torah shows that a dispute changes things.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that when there is a dispute
anointing is needed,
and it is not that whenever the king wants,
he passes the kingdom to his son?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּכִי אִיכָּא מַחְלוֹקֶת בָּעֵי מְשִׁיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source for the general rule, asks for the source of the exception from Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that a dispute over the throne requires anointing.

steps.title: 'He and his sons' only in peaceful times
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads 'he and his sons in the midst of ישראל' to mean the son inherits without anointing only when there is peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the פסוק says 'he and his sons in the midst of ישראל.' When there is peace in ישראל, we apply 'he and his sons' to him, even without anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from Step 25 using the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the midst of ישראל' are read as 'when ישראל is at peace.' Only then does the son inherit automatically. When there is a dispute, he needs anointing, which explains שלמה, יואש and יהואחז.

keyTerms.meaning: We apply the פסוק to him

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול always needs anointing, even if his father was כהן גדול. A king's son inherits without anointing, but only in peaceful times. If there is a dispute, he must be anointed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The verse says:
"He and his sons, in the midst of Israel."
When there is peace in Israel,
we apply to him "he and his sons,"
even without anointing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'In the midst of ישראל' means in peaceful times. Only then does the son inherit without anointing.

steps.title: Even יהוא was anointed only because of the dispute with יורם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that יהוא בן נמשי was anointed only because of יורם's challenge to his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Even יהוא בן נמשי was anointed only because of the dispute with יורם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds יהוא to the list of kings who were anointed because someone disputed their kingship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the rule from step 26: when there is a dispute over the throne, the king is anointed. The ברייתא says יהוא's anointing also came only because of a dispute, in his case with יורם.

phrases.english: It was taught: Even יהוא son of נמשי
was not anointed except
because of the dispute of יורם.
phrases.notes: יורם was the king יהוא replaced. See מלכים ב 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another example of the rule that a dispute over the throne requires anointing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהוא was anointed only because of the dispute with יורם.

steps.title: יהוא was first in his line, so why mention a dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: יהוא was the first king of his dynasty, so he should need anointing anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn that יהוא was anointed because he was the first king of his line!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Why give the dispute as the reason, when יהוא was a first king and a first king is always anointed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps taught that only a king's son skips anointing. יהוא was not a king's son, so he should have been anointed even with no dispute. The reason the ברייתא gives seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: let him derive it instead from a simpler reason
the first king of a dynasty

phrases.english: But let him derive it
because he is the first!
phrases.notes: He means יהוא started a new royal line. He was not the son of a king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason the ברייתא gave in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that יהוא was anointed only because of the dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A first king of a dynasty needs anointing anyway, so the dispute should not be needed as the reason.

steps.title: Kings of דוד's house are anointed; kings of ישראל are not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is missing words. It really teaches that kings from בית דוד are anointed, but kings of ישראל are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing something, and this is what it teaches: Kings of the house of דוד are anointed. Kings of ישראל are not anointed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא left out a line. Once that line is added, the question goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added rule is that kings of the northern kingdom of ישראל are never anointed, even if they are first kings. So יהוא would normally not be anointed at all. Only the dispute with יורם made it necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what it is teaching
kings of the northern kingdom of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Here מלכי ישראל does not mean every Jewish king. It means the kings of the northern kingdom, as opposed to דוד's line in יהודה.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
Kings of the house of דוד are anointed;
kings of ישראל are not anointed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by adding a missing line to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds missing words to the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהוא, as a first king, would need anointing anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: Kings of ישראל are never anointed, so only the dispute caused יהוא's anointing.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that kings of בית דוד are anointed but kings of ישראל are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the new rule. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 added a new rule that splits the two royal lines. A rule like that needs a source in the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know it?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that only kings of בית דוד are anointed.

steps.title: רבא: "this one" needs anointing, no other
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from "Arise, anoint him, for this is he" that דוד's line needs anointing and other kings do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, "Arise, anoint him, for this is he." This one needs anointing, and no other needs anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source. The word "this" in the פסוק about anointing דוד limits anointing to דוד's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "this" is read as a limit: anointing belongs to "this one," meaning דוד and his line. Kings from other lines, like the kings of ישראל, are left out.
steps.whatToRemember: Kings of בית דוד are anointed and kings of ישראל are not. That is why יהוא needed the special reason of a dispute.

phrases.english: רבא said: The verse says:
"Arise, anoint him, for this is he"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:12

phrases.english: this one requires anointing,
and no other requires anointing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "this" in שמואל א 16:12 limits anointing to דוד's line.

steps.title: Would we waste the holy oil just because of יורם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again and asks how the holy oil could be misused to anoint a king of ישראל just because of a dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Even יהוא בן נמשי was anointed only because of the dispute with יורם. But because of the dispute of יורם בן אחאב, should we misuse the holy oil?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the line from the ברייתא in order to challenge it. Using the holy anointing oil for a king who does not really need it seems like misusing holy property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 showed that kings of ישראל do not need anointing. So using the sacred oil on יהוא would be using holy oil for no proper purpose. A political dispute does not seem to justify that.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we commit מעילה, misusing holy property

phrases.english: The Master said:
Even יהוא son of נמשי
was not anointed except
because of the dispute of יורם.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשּׁוּם מַחְלוּקְתּוֹ שֶׁל יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב
phrases.english: And because of the dispute of יורם son of אחאב
shall we misuse the oil?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם מַחְלוּקְתּוֹ שֶׁל יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב נִמְעוֹל בְּשֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 27 and challenges it in light of the rule from step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that יהוא was anointed with the holy שמן המשחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king of ישראל does not need anointing, so using the holy oil on him would be misusing holy property.

steps.title: יהוא was anointed with pure balsam, not the holy oil
steps.stepSummary: As רב פפא said, the anointing was done with pure balsam. Here too, יהוא was anointed with pure balsam.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פפא said: with pure balsam. Here too, with pure balsam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יהוא was not anointed with the holy oil at all. He was anointed with plain pure balsam, so nothing holy was misused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anointing still showed that יהוא was the rightful king against יורם. But because it used ordinary balsam, there was no misuse of holy oil.

keyTerms.meaning: pure balsam oil (not the holy oil)

phrases.english: As רב פפא said:
phrases.notes: This points to another place where רב פפא said a king was anointed with balsam instead of the holy oil.

phrases.english: with pure balsam;
here too, with pure balsam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the anointing was done with
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהוא was anointed with the holy anointing oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was anointed with pure balsam, so no holy oil was misused.

steps.title: יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, his older brother
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, who was two years older than him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, who was two years older than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. It sets up a discussion about which brother was really older.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהואחז was a king's son, so normally he would not need anointing. But his older brother יהויקים could claim the throne, and that created a dispute. So יהואחז was anointed.

phrases.english: And יהואחז, because of יהויקים,
who was older than him by two years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a new example of a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהואחז was anointed because his older brother יהויקים disputed his kingship.

steps.title: But the פסוק calls יהואחז the firstborn!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a פסוק lists יוחנן as the firstborn, and רבי יוחנן says יוחנן is יהואחז. So יהואחז was older.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was יהויקים really older than him? But it is written: "And the sons of יאשיהו: the firstborn יוחנן, the second יהויקים, the third צדקיהו, the fourth שלום." And רבי יוחנן said: שלום is צדקיהו, and יוחנן is יהואחז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that יהויקים was older. A פסוק seems to show that יהואחז was the oldest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls יוחנן the firstborn and יהויקים the second. Since רבי יוחנן identifies יוחנן as יהואחז, יהואחז was the oldest. Then there was no older brother to cause a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: was he really older than him?

phrases.english: And was he older than him?
But isn't it written: "And the sons of יאשיהו:
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 3:15

phrases.english: the firstborn יוחנן, the second יהויקים,
the third צדקיהו, the fourth שלום",
and רבי יוחנן said:
שלום is the same as צדקיהו,
יוחנן is the same as יהואחז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 34 that יהויקים was older.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that יהויקים was two years older than יהואחז.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls יוחנן, who is יהואחז, the firstborn, so יהואחז was the oldest.

steps.title: "Firstborn" means first to reign
steps.stepSummary: יהויקים really was older. "Firstborn" means יהואחז was first in line for the kingship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, יהויקים was older. And what does "firstborn" mean? Firstborn for the kingship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is right: יהויקים was older. The word "firstborn" in the פסוק means first to become king, not first to be born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes the meaning of "firstborn" in the פסוק from birth order to order of reigning. That keeps the ברייתא's claim that יהויקים was older, so there was a real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: and what is the meaning of
first in line for the kingship

phrases.english: Actually, יהויקים was older,
and what is "firstborn"?
First for the kingship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35 by reinterpreting "firstborn."
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Firstborn" means born first, so יהואחז was the oldest.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Firstborn" means first to reign. יהויקים was older by birth.

steps.title: Can a younger son reign before an older one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק says יהושפט gave the kingdom to יהורם because he was the firstborn, so the oldest should reign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do younger sons reign before older sons? But it is written: "And he gave the kingdom to יהורם, because he was the firstborn"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. A פסוק shows that the kingdom goes to the oldest son, so how could younger יהואחז reign before יהויקים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives being firstborn as the reason יהורם got the throne. That suggests the older son always has the right to the kingship. Then the younger יהואחז should not have come first.

phrases.english: And do younger ones reign
before older ones?
But it is written:
"And the kingdom he gave to יהורם
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 21:3

phrases.english: because he was the firstborn"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָלְכִי זוּטְרֵי מִקַּמֵּי קַשִּׁישֵׁי? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 36, that the younger son reigned first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the younger יהואחז reigned before the older יהויקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about יהורם shows that the firstborn gets the throne, so the older son should reign first.

steps.title: יהורם was fit to fill his fathers' place; יהויקים was not
steps.stepSummary: יהורם was worthy to take his fathers' place, so as firstborn he got the throne. יהויקים was not worthy, so his younger brother reigned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהורם was fit to fill his fathers' place. יהויקים was not fit to fill his fathers' place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the oldest son gets the throne only if he is fit to be king. יהורם was fit, but יהויקים was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being firstborn gives a right to the throne only together with being suitable to rule. Since יהויקים was not suitable, the younger יהואחז was made king first. That explains both פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: fit to fill his fathers' place

steps.whatToRemember: The firstborn inherits the throne only if he is fit to fill his fathers' place. Otherwise a younger son may reign first, as יהואחז did ahead of יהויקים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a condition to inheriting the kingship. Being firstborn is not enough by itself; the son must also be worthy to rule.

phrases.english: יהורם was one who filled his fathers' place;

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹיָקִים לָאו מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו הֲוָה.
phrases.english: יהויקים was not one who filled his fathers' place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37 by telling apart the two cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The firstborn reigns first only when he is fit to fill his fathers' place. יהויקים was not, so יהואחז reigned first.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוחנן about the names of יאשיהו's sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן's statement from step 35, that שלום is צדקיהו and יוחנן is יהואחז, so it can examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He is שלום, he is צדקיהו; he is יוחנן, he is יהואחז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes רבי יוחנן's statement from step 35 so it can question it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 35, רבי יוחנן said that two pairs of names each belong to one person. שלום and צדקיהו are one king, and יוחנן and יהואחז are another. The next step will test the first pair against a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A son of יאשיהו, identified here with צדקיהו
The last king of the house of דוד

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This points back to what רבי יוחנן said a few lines earlier.

phrases.english: He is Shallum, he is Zedekiah;
he is Johanan, he is Jehoahaz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's statement from step 35 to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: שלום is צדקיהו, and יוחנן is יהואחז.

steps.title: The פסוק counts צדקיהו and שלום separately
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists צדקיהו as third and שלום as fourth, so they seem to be two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק counts them one by one, as it is written: 'the third... the fourth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement. The פסוק gives צדקיהו and שלום different numbers, which suggests they are two different sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one person had two names, why would the פסוק list him twice with two separate numbers? Counting them one by one sounds like counting two people. This seems to contradict the claim that שלום is צדקיהו.

phrases.english: But doesn't it count them one by one,
as it is written: "The third, the fourth"!
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 3:15. The third is צדקיהו and the fourth is שלום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification quoted in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שלום and צדקיהו are one person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק gives them separate numbers (third and fourth), which implies two people.

steps.title: Third among the sons, fourth among the kings
steps.stepSummary: 'Third' means צדקיהו was the third son. 'Fourth' means he was the fourth to become king, after יהואחז, יהויקים and יכניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'third'? Third among the sons. And what is 'fourth'? Fourth in the kingship. First יהואחז reigned, then יהויקים, then יכניה, then צדקיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two numbers describe the same person in two different ways. One counts his place among the sons, and the other counts his place among the kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is not counting two people. It tells us two facts about one man: he was born third, and he reigned fourth. Listing the four kings in order shows that צדקיהו really was the fourth to rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Third among the sons', his birth order
'Fourth in the kingship', his order as king
The king who reigned before צדקיהו

steps.whatToRemember: One person can get two numbers in a פסוק: third son, but fourth king.

phrases.english: What is "third"? Third among the sons,
and what is "fourth"? Fourth to the kingship.
For at first Jehoahaz reigned,
and afterward Jehoiakim,
and afterward Jeconiah,
phrases.notes: יכניה was a grandson of יאשיהו, not one of his sons, so he counts as a king but not as a son.

phrases.english: and afterward Zedekiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the numbers in the פסוק as two different counts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Third and fourth are two separate people in one list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both numbers describe צדקיהו: third by birth, fourth by reign.

steps.title: Why צדקיהו was called שלום: he was complete in his deeds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that he was called שלום because he was perfect (משולם) in his actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: He is שלום, he is צדקיהו. Why was he called שלום? Because he was perfect in his deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא repeats that שלום is צדקיהו and explains the name שלום. It says the name praises his good deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name שלום comes from the same root as משולם, which means 'complete' or 'perfect'. According to this explanation, the name is a compliment to his character.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
He is Shallum, he is Zedekiah.
And why was he called Shallum?
Because he was perfect in his deeds.
phrases.notes: מְשׁוּלָּם sounds like שַׁלּוּם. Both come from the word for 'complete'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that builds on the identification of שלום as צדקיהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He was called שלום because he was perfect in his deeds.

steps.title: Another reason for the name שלום: the kingdom of דוד ended in his days
steps.stepSummary: Some say he was called שלום because the kingship of the house of דוד came to its end (שֶׁשָּׁלְמָה) in his time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: 'שלום', because the kingdom of the house of דוד ended in his days.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different reason for the name שלום. It ties the name to the end of the kingdom of דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the same root means 'finished', not 'perfect'. So the name is not praise of his deeds. It marks him as the last king of דוד's line.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingship of the house of דוד

phrases.english: Some say: "Shallum" —
because the kingdom of the house of David was concluded in his days,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He was called שלום because דוד's kingdom ended in his days.

steps.title: What was his real name?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what his actual birth name was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was his name?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up the next move. Since שלום and צדקיהו are both titles, it asks for his original name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two explanations so far treat שלום as a descriptive name, so a real name must exist somewhere. The question opens the search for it.

phrases.english: And what was his name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the discussion of his names.

steps.title: His real name was מתניה
steps.stepSummary: His name was מתניה, as the פסוק says that the king of בבל crowned מתניה and changed his name to צדקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: His name was מתניה, as it says: 'The king of בבל crowned מתניה his uncle in his place, and changed his name to צדקיהו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that his real name was מתניה. It proves this from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that מתניה was his original name. It also shows that the name צדקיהו was given to him by the king of בבל. That raises the next question: why that particular name?

phrases.english: Mattaniah was his name,
as it is stated: "And the king of Babylon crowned
Mattaniah his uncle in his place,
phrases.notes: 'His uncle' means the uncle of יכניה, the king who was removed.

phrases.english: and changed his name to Zedekiah."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 24:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His name was מתניה, as shown in מלכים ב 24:17.

steps.title: Why נבוכדנצר named him צדקיהו
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר told him: God will justify the judgment against you if you rebel against me. A פסוק confirms that he rebelled despite an oath by God.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: God will declare the judgment against you just if you rebel against me. And it is written: 'He also rebelled against King נבוכדנצר, who had made him swear by God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the meaning of the new name צדקיהו. It was a warning from נבוכדנצר, and a פסוק shows that צדקיהו broke that oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צדקיהו is made of צדק ('justice') and יה ('God'). נבוכדנצר chose the name as a warning: if you rebel, God will show that your punishment is just. The second פסוק shows that צדקיהו did rebel, breaking an oath made in God's name.

keyTerms.meaning: 'God will declare the judgment against you just'

steps.whatToRemember: צדקיהו's real name was מתניה. 'שלום' describes him (perfect in deeds, or the last of דוד's kings), and 'צדקיהו' was נבוכדנצר's warning name: God will justify your punishment if you rebel.
steps.confusionAlert: It was נבוכדנצר, not God or a נביא, who gave the name צדקיהו and spoke these words to him.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: נבוכדנצר is speaking to מתניה.

phrases.english: God will justify the judgment against you
phrases.notes: It's a wordplay: צִדְקִיָּהוּ is built from צֶדֶק and יָהּ.

phrases.english: if you rebel against me,
(as it is stated: "And he brought him to Babylon")
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar,
who had made him swear by God."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 36:13

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָהּ יַצְדִּיק עָלֶיךָ אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the name change mentioned in the פסוק of step 45.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name צדקיהו meant that God would justify judgment against him if he rebelled, and he did rebel.
